speaker: Unknown
en: If you're giving up on your user interface, if you're giving up on evolving your experience for a customer, I think that's a brainless bet.
zh: 如果你放弃了你的用户界面，如果你放弃了为客户演进体验，我认为那是一个不动脑子的赌注。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think agents will replace all the interfaces.
zh: 我不认为智能体会取代所有的界面。

speaker: Unknown
en: For the first time in a long time, we're solving foundational design challenges again.
zh: 长久以来，我们第一次又是在解决基础性的设计难题。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is certainly some customer pushback in some places to quote unquote Chinese models.
zh: 当然，在某些地方，客户对所谓的“中国模型”存在一些抵触。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is not customer pushback to open models.
zh: 客户对开源模型没有抵触。

speaker: Unknown
en: The jury is really out on the benefits of building specialized models at the moment.
zh: 目前，构建专用模型的收益究竟如何，还远没有定论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right now, the production of technology is faster than the consumption of technology.
zh: 现在，技术的生产速度快于技术的消费速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're moving from a world of information asymmetry to imagination asymmetry.
zh: 我们正在从一个信息不对称的世界，转向一个想象力不对称的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is 20VC with me, Harry Stebbings.
zh: 这里是 20VC,我是 Harry Stebbings。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in today's show, we sit down with Mike Cannon-Brooks, founder and CEO at Atlassian, to discuss...
zh: 那么在今天的节目中，我们请来 Atlassian 的创始人兼 CEO Mike Cannon-Brooks,一起讨论……

speaker: Unknown
en: What happens to traditional software in a world where agents are able to extract information from databases?
zh: 在智能体能够从数据库中提取信息的世界里，传统软件会怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they still carry value?
zh: 它们还有价值吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where is enduring value in a world of agents?
zh: 在一个智能体的世界里，持久的价值在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: How does Atlassian think about building the context layer that will power enterprise AI agents?
zh: Atlassian 如何思考构建支撑企业级 AI 智能体的上下文层？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what does this mean for the next generation of enterprise software?
zh: 这对下一代企业软件意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: This and so much more in an incredibly revealing but also just awesome discussion with Mike.
zh: 这些以及更多内容，都在这场极具启发性、同时也非常精彩的与 Mike 的讨论中。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've known him for years.
zh: 我认识他已经很多年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's an incredible dude and this was so much fun to record.
zh: 他是个了不起的人，录制这期节目非常有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: But before we dive into the show today, Base44 is one of those products I used and I just thought straight away, man, I wish I'd had this when I started 20VC with $50 and no contacts in venture.
zh: 但在我们进入今天的节目之前，Base44 是我用过的产品之一，我立刻就想，天啊，真希望我当初创办 20VC 的时候就有它，那时我只有 50 美元，在风投圈里也没有任何人脉。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wanted to see what it could do, so I built a guest research hub for the show.
zh: 我想看看它能做什么，所以我为这个节目搭建了一个嘉宾研究中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Upcoming guests, company notes, previous interviews, sponsor contacts, follow-ups, all in one amazing location.
zh: 即将到来的嘉宾、公司笔记、过往访谈、赞助商联系方式、后续跟进，全部集中在一个超棒的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: I described it in plain English.
zh: 我只是用大白话描述了一下需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: A few minutes later, I had the product open in front of me.
zh: 几分钟后，这个产品就展现在我眼前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Database, login, backend and hosting already handled and just all in one.
zh: 数据库、登录、后端和托管都已处理好，而且全都集成在一处。

speaker: Unknown
en: It made it so easy.
zh: 它让这一切变得如此简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what I loved.
zh: 这就是我喜欢它的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't write a long spec.
zh: 我没有写一份冗长的规格说明。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't stitch five different tools together.
zh: 我没有把五个不同的工具拼凑在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: I built the thing and I started using it.
zh: 我把东西做出来，然后就开始用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: For any founder listening, that's the point.
zh: 对于正在收听的每一位创始人，这就是重点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The faster you turn an idea into something real, the faster you launch.
zh: 你越快把一个想法变成真实的东西，你就能越快地发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: Apps, dashboards, internal systems, AI agents, whatever you need to build, Base44 gets you there.
zh: 应用、仪表盘、内部系统、AI 智能体，无论你需要构建什么，Base44 都能帮你实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go to Base44.com forward slash 20VC.
zh: 访问 Base44.com/20VC。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's Base44.com slash 20VC.
zh: 也就是 Base44.com/20VC。

speaker: Unknown
en: While Base44 helps you build faster, Laredin helps you measure AI impact.
zh: Base44 帮你更快地构建，而 Laredin 帮你衡量 AI 的影响力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every company now runs two workforces, humans and AI agents.
zh: 现在每家公司都拥有两支劳动力大军：人类和 AI 智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Laredin is the first unified dashboard across both workforces that measures their work and optimizes their impact.
zh: Laredin 是首个横跨这两支劳动力大军的统一仪表盘，衡量它们的工作并优化其影响力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Laredin answers four questions.
zh: Laredin 回答四个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who's using AI?
zh: 谁在使用 AI?

speaker: Unknown
en: Which tools?
zh: 使用哪些工具？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it costing?
zh: 成本是多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's it actually being produced for every team across every vendor?
zh: 以及对每个团队、每个供应商来说，它实际产出了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: AI ROI stops being a guess and becomes a number that you can consistently and confidently measure.
zh: AI 的投资回报率不再靠猜，而是变成一个你可以持续、有信心地衡量的数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: Gainsight, Vertiv, SurveyMonkey, and many other enterprise organizations run their AI programs on Laredin.
zh: Gainsight、Vertiv、SurveyMonkey 以及许多其他企业组织都在 Laredin 上运行他们的 AI 项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thousands of AI tools and millions of dollars of AI spend are measured.
zh: 数千种 AI 工具和数百万美元的 AI 支出得到衡量。

speaker: Unknown
en: You bet on AI, Laredin proves that it's working.
zh: 你押注了 AI,Laredin 证明它正在发挥作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit Laredin.com to learn more.
zh: 访问 Laredin.com 了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's L-A-R-R-I-D-I-N dot com.
zh: 也就是 L-A-R-R-I-D-I-N.com。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have now arrived at your destination.
zh: 你已经到达目的地。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mike, dude, I love our conversations.
zh: Mike,老兄，我太喜欢我们的对话了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are always my favorite.
zh: 它们一直是我最喜欢的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thank you so much for joining me today.
zh: 所以非常感谢你今天来参加节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, thanks for having me back, man.
zh: 哦,谢谢你能邀请我回来,伙计。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's appreciated getting invited back.
zh: 能被邀请回来很感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: I must give those interesting answers.
zh: 我肯定给出了那些有趣的回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw your little rant the other day.
zh: 我前几天看到了你那段小吐槽。

speaker: Unknown
en: I loved it.
zh: 我很喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: You give honest answers, which I don't always get.
zh: 你会给出诚实的回答,而我并不总能得到这样的回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that I really want to start on is we see a world of agents and agents remove a lot of human need and interaction with data providers or data sources.
zh: 我真正想开始聊的是,我们看到一个智能体的世界,智能体消除了大量对数据提供者或数据源的人类需求和交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about a world where value shifts as agents retrieve and do tasks for us and the potential for an Atlassian to be a data provider, not a doer?
zh: 当智能体为我们检索和执行任务、以及 Atlassian 有可能成为数据提供者而不是执行者时,价值随之转移,你怎么看待这样的世界?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there is some premise to the question that's slightly incorrect.
zh: 我认为这个问题里有一些前提稍微不正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, look, I can see for certain tasks that is the case.
zh: 我认为,你看,对于某些任务,我确实能看到情况是这样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where the tasks are very functional, that is the case.
zh: 在任务非常功能化的地方,情况确实如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where the tasks have a lot of taste and interaction and collaboration involved, I don't think that will be the case, certainly not in the same way.
zh: 而在任务涉及大量品味、交互和协作的地方,我不认为会是这样,至少不会以同样的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's very hard to give an answer across all types of tasks.
zh: 所以很难对所有类型的任务给出一个统一的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, one might ask, there are certain types of shopping, if you take a consumer task, not something that we do, obviously, so a Premier Safe example.
zh: 你知道,有人可能会问,某些类型的购物,拿一个消费者任务来说,显然不是我们做的事,所以这是个 Premier Safe 式的无风险例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are certain types of shopping I just want to get the thing and move on.
zh: 有某些类型的购物,我只是想拿到那个东西然后继续前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm buying, I don't know, charging cable off Amazon, just give me the charging cable.
zh: 如果我在买,我不知道,在亚马逊上买一根充电线,直接给我充电线就行。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't care.
zh: 我不在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't need anything, right?
zh: 我不需要任何别的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And if there are other types of shopping where I may enjoy the experience, I may want to go to the store, I want to do a lot of research, I want to do it myself.
zh: 而还有其他类型的购物,我可能会享受这个过程,我可能想去店里,我想做很多研究,我想自己来做。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's going to be a whole range of things.
zh: 会有一整个范围的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, yes, for some tasks, it's going to get rid of the pedestrian.
zh: 所以,是的,对于某些任务,它会消除那些平庸乏味的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just want to get the thing done.
zh: 我只是想把事情搞定。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in the enterprise collaboration world and in the business workflow world, agents are going to help and are already helping, I would argue, in a lot of cases, move the work forward to let people honestly focus on higher value, creative parts of the job.
zh: 但在企业协作世界和业务工作流世界里,智能体会帮忙——而且我会说,在很多情况下已经在帮忙——推动工作前进,让人们诚实地专注于工作中更高价值、更有创造性的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that will change a lot of jobs, but I don't think it's necessarily negative, nor do I think it's bad for Atlassian.
zh: 我认为这会改变很多工作,但我不认为这必然是负面的,我也不认为这对 Atlassian 是坏事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's great for Atlassian.
zh: 我认为这对 Atlassian 是好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we want to help be a part of that agentic world.
zh: 所以我们想帮助成为那个智能体世界的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the experiences of how we do that is a long way from solved and settled in enterprise software.
zh: 但在企业软件中,我们如何做到这一点的体验还远未得到解决和定型。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I were to ask you on the flip side of that, what is the core strategic decision that will determine the success of Atlassian in the next 12 months?
zh: 如果我反问你,在接下来的 12 个月里,决定 Atlassian 成败的核心战略决策是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: What would your answer be?
zh: 你的答案会是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, I'm well on record.
zh: 是的,我早已有公开记录。

speaker: Unknown
en: Headless is brainless by definition.
zh: 无头的在定义上就是无脑的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, I think, again, we're confusing- You've said this before, Mike.
zh: 你看,我认为,再说一次,我们是在混淆——你以前说过这话,Mike。

speaker: Unknown
en: You stand by that?
zh: 你还坚持这个说法吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 绝对坚持。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because when people talk about headless in that way, if you're giving up on your user interface, if you're giving up on evolving your experience for a customer to solve the problems that you set out to solve for them, if you are not a significant part of that experience, yes, I think that's a brainless bet.
zh: 因为当人们那样谈论无头时,如果你放弃了自己的用户界面,如果你放弃了为客户演进你的体验以解决你当初要为他们解决的问题,如果你不是那个体验的重要组成部分,是的,我认为那是一个无脑的赌注。

speaker: Unknown
en: That does not mean we're not big on MCP.
zh: 那并不意味着我们不大力投入 MCP。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not big on CLIs.
zh: 我们并不是不重视 CLI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we have one of the top five, top three MCP servers in the world.
zh: 我认为我们拥有世界前五、前三的 MCP 服务器之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we're hugely big on MCP and its ability to allow agents and harnesses to contribute data to our platform and to the teamwork graph and to read data from the teamwork graph.
zh: 就像我们极其重视 MCP 及其让智能体和 harness 向我们的平台、向 teamwork graph 写入数据以及从 teamwork graph 读取数据的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it shows off, to be honest, MCP and harnesses show off the results of our graph, right?
zh: 而且说实话,它展示了,MCP 和 harness 展示了我们图的结果,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: How great quality our context graph is to solve all manner of problems for our customers.
zh: 我们的上下文图的质量有多高,能为我们的客户解决各种各样的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's great.
zh: 而这很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if our interfaces and our design is not evolving to solve some problems or some significant part of the problem set better for the customer, then yes, I think you're going to be in trouble.
zh: 但如果我们的界面和我们的设计没有在为客户更好地解决某些问题或问题集中某个重要部分上演进,那么是的,我认为你会陷入麻烦。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then you fundamentally disagree then that in a world of agents, interface and design becomes less important?
zh: 那么你是从根本上不同意,在智能体的世界里,界面和设计会变得不那么重要?

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 绝对不同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it becomes more important.
zh: 我认为它变得更重要了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think design and experience is one of the keys to success in the AI era.
zh: 我认为设计和体验是 AI 时代成功的关键之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we are massively invested in design and experience at the moment in a way that we never have been before.
zh: 就像我们现在在设计上的投入是巨大的,是我们从未有过的程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've always been quite a large investor in design and experience.
zh: 我们一直是设计和体验方面相当大的投资者。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have continued to upgrade our experience in a way that I would say few enterprise software vendors have done over the last 20 years.
zh: 我们持续升级我们的体验，可以说，过去 20 年里很少有企业软件厂商做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really easy to make an app, I always think, with a current, you know, say, better than 90% of apps out there today, that's easy.
zh: 如今做一个应用真的很容易，我一直觉得，做得比今天市面上 90% 的应用都好，这很容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in five years time, that app will be better than 20%.
zh: 但五年之后，那个应用只会比 20% 的好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, experience degrades as we have higher and higher standards.
zh: 你知道，随着我们的标准越来越高，体验是会退化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: To upgrade app experiences is really hard.
zh: 要升级应用体验真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: It takes a lot of work, it takes a lot of R&D, it takes a lot of
zh: 这需要大量的工作，需要大量的研发，需要大量的

speaker: Unknown
en: Difficult craft work to continue to do that.
zh: 艰难的匠心工艺才能持续做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in an era where we're all going to need to up level our experiences to handle the AI era.
zh: 我们正处于这样一个时代：我们都需要提升我们的体验，以应对 AI 时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do think design experience is even more important in the AI era.
zh: 但我确实认为，在 AI 时代，设计体验甚至更加重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it will be the differentiator.
zh: 我认为它将成为差异化因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you argue that technology creation is increasingly cheap, technology creation is abundant and verdant, the differentiators, to me, clearly one of them will be design and experience, will be what makes you stand out as an application or as a product or a service.
zh: 如果你说技术创造越来越便宜，技术创造充足而繁茂，那么差异化因素——在我看来，其中一个显然会是设计和体验，它将是让你作为一个应用、一个产品或一个服务脱颖而出的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you don't think we'll have horizontal agents which stretch across a number of different vertical providers and do functional work for us.
zh: 所以你不认为我们会有横跨多个不同垂直提供商、为我们做功能性工作的横向智能体吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You think the design and the experience of those vertical providers will remain incredibly strong.
zh: 你认为那些垂直提供商的设计和体验仍将保持非常强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is not a leading question, by the way.
zh: 顺便说一句，这不是一个引导性的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't, I, it's a too simplistic view of the world.
zh: 我不，我，这是对世界过于简单化的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we will certainly have some horizontal agents that handle a breadth of tasks.
zh: 我认为我们当然会有一些处理广泛任务的横向智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you will also have vertical agents that go very deep in a singular task.
zh: 我认为你也会有一些在单一任务上钻研得非常深的垂直智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think agents will replace all the interfaces.
zh: 我不认为智能体会取代所有的界面。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think all three of these can be true at the same time.
zh: 我认为这三者可以同时成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as an example, we have lots of agents that run in a lot of platforms from, you know, obviously Claude and Codex and Cursor and places like this and Teams and Slack that access the Alassian platform and contribute data back to the Alassian platform.
zh: 举个例子，我们有很多智能体运行在许多平台上，比如显然有 Claude 和 Codex 和 Cursor 以及这类地方，还有 Teams 和 Slack，它们访问 Alassian 平台，并把数据回传到 Alassian 平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: That does not mean that's the best interface to do all the jobs on the Atlassian platform.
zh: 这并不意味着那就是在 Atlassian 平台上完成所有工作的最佳界面。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can be very useful for a lot of different things and vice versa.
zh: 它在很多不同的事情上都可能非常有用，反之亦然。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're announcing a lot of features with our partner Figma, for example, and another set of features with our partner Databricks.
zh: 例如，我们正在与合作伙伴 Figma 宣布很多功能，与合作伙伴 Databricks 宣布另一组功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: In both cases, allowing you to get to Figma functionality and Databricks functionality from within the Atlassian platform is really powerful.
zh: 在这两种情况下，让你能够在 Atlassian 平台内部使用 Figma 的功能和 Databricks 的功能，是非常强大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm reading a conference page and I want to just select a piece of text and say, can you check this number for me?
zh: 如果我在读一个会议页面，我只想选中一段文字，然后说，你能帮我核对一下这个数字吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it goes off to Databricks or to Snowflake through the Teemo Graphs data context and gets you back the answer or gives you a small chart.
zh: 然后它通过 Teemo Graphs 的数据上下文去到 Databricks 或 Snowflake，给你拿回答案，或者给你一个小图表。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's great.
zh: 那很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not saying Confluence is a BI tool.
zh: 那并不是说 Confluence 是一个 BI 工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it's not going to be the power of what you need, but sometimes when you want a quick answer retrieved from somewhere else, it is a very different experience than if I wanted to live in that world doing that thing.
zh: 它不会具备你所需要的那种强大能力，但有时候，当你想从别处快速获取一个答案时，那和我想生活在那个世界里做那件事，是非常不同的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Same with Figma as an example, right?
zh: Figma 也是一样，对吧？

en: It's to use the best model for the best job.
zh: 而是为最适合的工作用最好的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Blending all the models for the best price for the customer and to get the outcome they want, right?
zh: 把所有模型以对客户最好的价格混合起来，达成他们想要的结果，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Applying the AI is our job.
zh: 应用 AI 才是我们的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if there is customer pushback to something like a Chinese model, quote unquote, that is something that we have to be very careful of.
zh: 但如果客户对所谓的「中国模型」之类的东西有抵触，那是我们必须非常谨慎对待的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we don't use any Chinese models in production.
zh: 所以我们在生产环境中不使用任何中国模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're very clear about that.
zh: 这一点我们非常明确。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what people don't understand is the distillation and the back and forth where knowing it's a Chinese model is kind of really interesting, but a lot of the US models are increasingly using Chinese models to train themselves, but they don't say that.
zh: 我认为人们没有理解的是蒸馏和来回的过程——知道它是个中国模型这一点其实挺有意思，但很多美国模型越来越多地用中国模型来训练自己，只是它们不说。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you end up with all these weird loops where I'm like, I don't know if that disappears over time.
zh: 于是你最后会陷入这些奇怪的循环，我会想，我不知道这种情况会不会随着时间消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: I suspect it does, but I think we'll have to see and watch.
zh: 我猜会，但我觉得我们得观察走着瞧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do talk to customers sometimes and say, do you use Linux?
zh: 我有时候会和客户谈，问，你们用 Linux 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they say, yes.
zh: 他们说，用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I say, is that European?
zh: 我说，那是欧洲的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they say, yes.
zh: 他们说，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I say, well...
zh: 我说，那么……

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's like 40% of contributions to something like this is quite high nowadays come from China because there are some amazing software engineers in China doing all sorts of things.
zh: 我认为如今像这类东西大约 40% 的贡献相当高比例来自中国，因为中国有很多出色的软件工程师在做各种各样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But because it's open source, we think, oh, well, someone's like checking all of that.
zh: 但因为它是开源的，我们就会想，哦，总有人在检查这一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, weirdly, with AI, we can check that even better than we ever have been able to before.
zh: 而实际上，很奇妙的是，有了 AI，我们比以往任何时候都更能进行检查。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're happy to use Linux.
zh: 而且他们很乐意用 Linux。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you think the skepticism is overwrought?
zh: 那么你认为这种怀疑态度是过度了？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a geopolitical issue around who has this sort of strategic control of the world.
zh: 我认为围绕谁来掌握对世界的战略控制权，存在一个地缘政治问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is a different issue from, should we use a model that was trained in China or by Chinese nationals?
zh: 那和「我们该不该用一个在中国训练的或由中国公民训练的模型」是不同的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some version of these two are very different questions, if you know what I mean, in terms of who's run the world, America versus China.
zh: 这两个问题的某种版本是非常不同的问题，如果你明白我的意思，就是关于谁主导世界，美国还是中国。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a big question.
zh: 那是个大问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's out of my league.
zh: 那超出了我的能力范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sorry.
zh: 抱歉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Years ago, you remember when you first met me, I was like, Harry Potter.
zh: 多年前，你还记得你第一次见我的时候，我说的是哈利·波特。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they're kind of one and the same because the people building the models are not able to leave and their families are not able to leave without letting the government know where they are going, when they are going.
zh: 但它们其实有点是一回事，因为构建模型的人没办法离开，他们的家人也没办法在不让政府知道他们去哪、什么时候走的情况下离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they are actually merging.
zh: 所以它们实际上正在合并。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'm not commenting on any of the social issues or other issues in that area.
zh: 但我不会评论那个领域的任何社会问题或其他问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I'm saying is from a technological perspective, for someone to say, I'm not going to use a piece of technology that is open, right?
zh: 我要说的是,从技术角度来看,如果有人说,我不会使用一项开放的技术,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm saying I'm not going to use this piece of open source code, I'm like, but I have the code.
zh: 如果我说我不会用这段开源代码,我会觉得,可是代码就在我手里啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, if you choose not to use it in your choice, that's totally fine.
zh: 好吧,如果你选择不用它,这是你的选择,那完全没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's your choice.
zh: 那是你的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for an enterprise to say, I'm not going to use a cheaper alternative that'll give me better results, when I know what's in it, I think is going to be a very hard long term choice.
zh: 但如果一家企业说,我不会使用一个更便宜、能给我更好结果、而且我清楚里面装了什么的替代方案,我认为这将是一个非常艰难的长期选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I suspect people are going to take those open weight models, which they are already doing, and fine tune and train them and call them their own.
zh: 而且我怀疑人们会拿那些开放权重模型——他们已经在这么做了——去微调、训练它们,然后称之为自己的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of the people who are training their own model, Large Company X claims they've built amazing model for purpose Y and it's got some wacky name.
zh: 大多数自己训练模型的人,某大公司 X 声称他们为一个特定目的 Y 构建了惊人的模型,还起了个古怪的名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've seen many, many times.
zh: 这种事我们已经见过太多次了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Almost every single time, that is, if it's not Nemotron, which it's usually not, it is a Chinese model that they've trained or added their own fine tuning specialization on top of, and then they call it their own model.
zh: 几乎每一次,如果不是 Nemotron——通常都不是——那就是一个他们训练过的中国模型,或者在它之上加了自己的微调特化,然后称之为自己模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, hang on, that's bullshit.
zh: 我就想说,等一下,那是胡扯。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is the same thing, right?
zh: 那是同一回事,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You've added to it and you've tweaked it.
zh: 你在它之上做了增补,你做了调整。

speaker: Unknown
en: You haven't trained it from scratch.
zh: 你并没有从零开始训练它。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was actually going to be my question, which is like, you know, we've seen Harvey and I think it's Ramp talk about the benefits that they've seen from building their own models.
zh: 这其实本来是我的问题,就是,你知道,我们看到 Harvey,还有我记得是 Ramp,谈到他们从构建自己的模型中获得的好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: You very clearly said last year that that wasn't a strategic focus for you and that you weren't going to go down that route.
zh: 你去年非常明确地说过,那不是你的战略重点,你不会走那条路。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, with the benefit of hindsight, has your thinking changed when you see all of these companies come out and talk about the benefits of building their own models?
zh: 那么,现在有了后见之明,当你看到所有这些公司站出来谈论构建自己模型的好处时,你的想法有变化吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you been validated?
zh: 你觉得自己被验证了吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: How has that thought process changed?
zh: 这个思考过程是怎么变化的?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a great question.
zh: 这是个好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: The jury is really out on the benefits of building specialized models at the moment.
zh: 目前,构建专用模型的好处还没有定论。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are definitely cases where specialized models are doing really well.
zh: 确实有一些专用模型表现非常出色的案例。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of the people building specialized models, I would argue, are not in those cases, though.
zh: 不过我认为,大多数构建专用模型的人并不属于那些案例。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are certainly, if you have a lot of proprietary data, if you have very specialized applications, there are definitely approaches to that, right?
zh: 当然,如果你有大量专有数据,如果你有非常专门的应用场景,那确实是有相应办法的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're doing, you know, certain robotics, for example, and world model, there's a lot of reasons why people are actually doing it that makes sense to me.
zh: 比如你在做某些机器人技术,还有世界模型,有很多人在做这件事的理由在我看来是合理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of others that I don't think will stand the test of time.
zh: 还有很多其他情况,我认为经不起时间的考验。

speaker: Unknown
en: They may have, at the time of shipping, a price performance benefit for a specific application.
zh: 在发布时,对于一个特定应用,它们可能有性价比优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: True.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Will that price performance hold up over time?
zh: 但这个性价比能经得起时间的考验吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not sure it will, as generalized models get better and better and better for a lot of applications, firstly.
zh: 我不确定它能,首先,随着通用模型越来越好越来越好,对很多应用来说是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Secondly, a lot of people who say they've trained their own model, I think they're being a little bit fast and loose with words as far as I'm concerned.
zh: 其次,很多说自己训练了自己模型的人,在我看来,他们在用词上有点轻率和随意。

speaker: Unknown
en: We could say we've trained a bunch of models at Atlassian.
zh: 我们也可以说我们在 Atlassian 训练了一堆模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I say that's bullshit.
zh: 我会说那是胡扯。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a bunch of very specialized openweight models that we fine tune
zh: 我们有一堆非常专门的开放权重模型,我们对它们做了微调,

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in tune for particular purposes that give great price performance for our customers that I don't claim to be our own model, I would say.
zh: 针对特定目的做了微调,为我们的客户提供了很好的性价比,但我不会宣称那是我们自己的模型,我会这么说。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that's where I think the claim is often vastly overweighted.
zh: 就是说,我认为这种宣称往往被极大地夸大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of these people are taking a Chinese model, generally, applying some domain-specific intelligence,
zh: 这些人中的大多数,通常是拿一个中国模型,施加一些领域特定的智能,

speaker: Unknown
en: You see they train them for like a million bucks and I'm like, there's no way you train this for a million bucks.
zh: 你会看到他们说花了一百万美元训练它们,我就会想,你不可能只花一百万美元训练出这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You took someone's billion dollar model and tailored it, if you want to think about it generically, for a particular application.
zh: 你是拿了别人花费数十亿美元打造的模型,然后把它改造得适合某个特定应用——如果你泛泛地这么理解的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's totally fine, but that's not really training your own model, I would say, right?
zh: 那完全没问题,但那并不是真正训练自己的模型,我会这么说,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're not starting with raw data, if that's their definition, then we do that a bunch in a bunch of different places, but it's not my definition of building a model from scratch.
zh: 如果你不是从原始数据开始——如果那是他们的定义的话——那我们在很多不同的地方都做过很多次,但那不是我对从零开始构建模型的定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: What, if it played out, would prove that thesis and your conviction to be wrong?
zh: 什么情况一旦发生,会证明这个论点和你坚信的东西是错的?

speaker: Unknown
en: They could continue to show exponential gains over and above using the latest foundational model on a sort of price per watt basis.
zh: 它们可以在每瓦价格之类的基础上,持续展现出超过使用最新基础模型的指数级收益。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we are seeing many more applications
zh: 所以我们看到的应用越来越多

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's very hard to answer these questions generically because it depends on the target application, actually, and the time to answer or solve a problem or a question, the cost and the period of time you're in.
zh: 而且要泛泛地回答这些问题其实很难,因为这取决于目标应用,以及回答或解决一个问题所需的时间和成本,还有你所处的时间段。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at an agentic harness, it is a way of applying a set of prompts and configurations, if you want to think about them that way, to a certain type of model and reapplying it many, many times, if you want to think about it as looping, so that you can get much more value out of a given class of model.
zh: 如果你看一个智能体框架,它本质上是一种把一组提示词和配置——如果你愿意这么理解的话——应用到某一类模型上,并反复重新应用很多很多次的方式,如果你愿意把它理解成循环,这样你就能从给定的一类模型中获得更多的价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yes, if you apply better models, you get better results from a lot of those harnesses.
zh: 而且没错,如果你用上更好的模型,很多这类框架确实能带来更好的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And harness design is really, really important nowadays, but it's not model progress.
zh: 如今框架设计真的非常非常重要,但那不是模型进步。

speaker: Unknown
en: These specialized models have to prove that they can stay ahead of the generified model for a given price performance ratio.
zh: 这些专用模型必须证明,在给定的性价比之下,它们能持续领先于通用化模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think I see many of them doing that.
zh: 我不认为我看到它们中的很多做到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Certainly not the vast majority of them doing that because you would need to have a continued specialized dataset and a problem that doesn't get generified away.
zh: 当然,绝大多数都没做到,因为你需要有一个持续的专用数据集,和一个不会被通用化所消解的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many people who I think had startups, hopefully none of whom you've invested in, that were building their own models two or three years ago, I think now the foundation models have just basically smashed what they do, right?
zh: 很多人——希望其中没有你投过的——两三年前在自建自己的模型,我觉得现在基础模型基本上已经把他们做的事情碾压了,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the quality of the generic model has improved far faster than their ability to stay ahead with whatever specialization they were doing.
zh: 通用模型的质量提升速度,远远超过了他们凭借自己做的那点专业化保持领先的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think I would need to see the reverse of that.
zh: 所以我觉得我需要看到相反的情况才会改变看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Luckily, none of my companies have, so great relief.
zh: 幸运的是,我的公司里没有一家是这样,所以非常欣慰。

speaker: Unknown
en: The question that I have on cost is, Mike, it's actually a joke we have with founders that I interview, because I interview a lot of very fast-growing company CEOs, and they're all private.
zh: 我在成本上的问题是——Mike,这其实是我和创业者之间的一个玩笑,因为我采访很多增长非常快的公司 CEO,他们都是私有的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I go, how do you think about the cost trade-off, Frontier versus Open, where maybe there's a little bit of a detriment in performance?
zh: 我会问:你怎么权衡成本,Frontier 还是 Open,也许性能上会有一点损失?

speaker: Unknown
en: And they go, you're kidding me, dude.
zh: 他们说:你开玩笑吧,老兄。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've seen how much money I've raised.
zh: 你没看到我融了多少钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're always like, can you take that bit out?
zh: 然后他们总是说:你能把那段剪掉吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: But I give a shit about cost.
zh: 我才在乎成本呢。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, you do.
zh: 不,你在乎的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you're a public.
zh: 我是说,你是上市公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about that without the luxury of, give a shit, I'm private and I've raised a bunch of money?
zh: 在没有「我在乎什么成本,我是私有的而且融了一大笔钱」这种奢侈条件的情况下,你怎么看这件事?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I love all these private companies that have raised a bunch of money and don't have to care about cost because they're not building the discipline to care about cost.
zh: 我是说,我喜欢这些融了一大笔钱、不用在乎成本的私有公司,因为他们没有在建立在乎成本的纪律。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of them do, but over time, discipline is really important.
zh: 有些公司在乎,但随着时间推移,纪律真的非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything you do in life, it's about discipline at some level, right?
zh: 人生中你做的任何事,在某种程度上都是关于纪律的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But what if your product is two to 3% off theirs because they have the ill discipline to always do Frontier?
zh: 但如果你的产品比他们的差百分之二到三,因为他们不守纪律、永远用 Frontier 呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess that depends if you continue to fund them and believe they'll be funded forever.
zh: 我想这取决于你是否继续给他们融资,并相信他们会被永远融资下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems unlikely given the history of technology, but maybe.
zh: 从技术的历史来看,这似乎不太可能,但也许吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think cost is really important, but it's not just because of that.
zh: 我认为成本真的很重要,但不仅仅是因为那个原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if you look at a lot of examples out there, it's very easy to use a very expensive model to get pretty good results pretty fast.
zh: 我认为如果你看看外面的很多例子,用一个很贵的模型很快得到相当不错的结果,是很容易的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think using a cheaper model or an older model and getting good at applying that to problem sets is a real advantage for most technologies and prices and costs.
zh: 我认为用一个更便宜的模型或更老的模型,并擅长把它应用到问题上,对大多数技术和价格与成本来说,是真正的优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think customers that we spoke to, so large enterprises around the world, they're incredibly sensitive to this type of stuff nowadays.
zh: 我觉得和我们交谈过的客户,也就是世界各地的大型企业,他们如今对这类东西极其敏感。

speaker: Unknown
en: They really, really care about the price performance.
zh: 他们真的、真的非常在乎性价比。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are increasingly doing so.
zh: 而且他们越来越在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a whole raft of products now that will show you your token spend either across the board in terms of your talent, either in DX and your engineering organization, right?
zh: 我们现在有一整套产品,可以向展示你的 token 花费——无论是全面地看你的团队,还是看 DX 和你的工程组织,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Understanding where you use which model, where you're getting value, which features you're using it for, where you should change to optimize your spending.
zh: 了解你在哪里用哪个模型,在哪里获得了价值,在哪些功能上使用它,以及应该在哪里做出改变来优化你的支出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because this is a bigger and bigger budget item and they see it's only going to be a bigger budget item and so they have to care about the spending.
zh: 因为这是一个越来越大的预算项目,而且他们看到它只会变成更大的预算项目,所以他们必须在乎这笔支出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now that I don't think is any different for them buying a generic model or a foundational model of any of the big three or four or five as it is buying a product where their costs are going to be backed into whatever that product they're buying is.
zh: 现在在我看来,这对他们购买通用模型或三五家大公司中任何一家的基础模型,与购买一个成本被捆绑进所购产品中的产品来说,没有任何区别。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that cost discipline is going to arrive continually more and more.
zh: 所以我认为成本纪律会不断越来越多地到来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's a strength of ours, for example, in how we are able to use our FinOps strength to continue to reduce the price of features that are used heavily.
zh: 而且我认为这是我们的一个优势,比如我们能够利用我们的 FinOps 优势,持续降低被大量使用的功能的价格。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that is a core strength and attribute of a great technology company will be its ability to manage technological costs.
zh: 我认为,一家伟大技术公司的核心优势和特质,将是它管理技术成本的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that would be routed in an intelligent model routing on a per task basis to optimize cost?
zh: 那这会立足于按任务进行智能模型路由以优化成本吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Model routing, model blending, applying the right model at the right time, using the right harness that, again, picks and adjusts itself.
zh: 模型路由、模型混合,在合适的时机应用合适的模型,使用合适的 harness——再说一次,它会自我挑选和调整。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a real burden area of exploration right now, right?
zh: 这是当前一个非常热门的探索领域,对吧?

speaker: Unknown

en: So, I mean, if you mean am I lonely in terms of, man, I have an awesome executive team and I work with 10,000 of the smartest people, no.
zh: 所以，我的意思是，如果你问的是我在孤独这个意义上，就是说，天哪，我有一个很棒的高管团队，我和一万名最聪明的人共事，不孤独。

speaker: Unknown
en: I always say that I get to work with an incredible number of very smart people on a daily basis solving hard problems.
zh: 我总是说，我每天都能和非常多非常聪明的人一起解决难题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you designed a job for me, I'd be like, that is what I want to do for the rest of my life.
zh: 如果你为我设计一份工作，我会说，这就是我想余生都做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you mean in terms of Scott, I see him frequently.
zh: 如果你指的是 Scott,我经常见到他。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not like he doesn't live like I'm in Amsterdam at the moment and he travels a bit as well.
zh: 不像他不住在附近那样，比如我现在在阿姆斯特丹，他也会到处出差。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like, I don't know, we hang out at least monthly and we drink wine or beer and talk about Atlassian and software and AI within the first three minutes of what's going on.
zh: 但是，我不知道，我们至少每个月都会聚一次，喝点葡萄酒或啤酒，聊 Atlassian、软件和 AI,开场三分钟内就会聊到最近的动态。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not like he is uninterested in what we're doing.
zh: 他并不是对我们正在做的事不感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not like I don't get near daily text messages.
zh: 也不是说我收不到几乎每天发来的短信。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why aren't we doing this?
zh: 我们为什么不做这个？

speaker: Unknown
en: So he's very active for a retired person, which is great.
zh: 所以对一个退休的人来说，他非常活跃，这很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: You got years of experience, but everyone has their own journey to run, right?
zh: 你有多年经验，但每个人都有自己要走的路，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's okay.
zh: 我觉得这没什么问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what I was trying to say beforehand is you have to understand where your energy comes from.
zh: 我想我之前想说的是，你必须明白你的能量来自哪里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's one of the things that I want to make sure I get across to my kids is figure out what it is that gives you energy and try to do more of that thing and you'll be okay in life, just in a generalized world, right?
zh: 我想这是我想确保传达给我孩子们的事情之一：搞清楚是什么给你能量，尽量多做那件事，这样你的人生就会过得不错，泛泛而言，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of those people you talked about, and I get it in the AI era, man, the mental health challenges of being a founder have long been written about and have never been written about enough.
zh: 我想你提到的那些人——我明白，在 AI 时代，天哪，作为创始人的心理健康挑战早已有人写过，而且永远写得不够多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think because it's a very stressful job to feel like you have other people's livelihood and less so at sort of my time.
zh: 我觉得因为这是一份压力非常大的工作，感觉你背负着其他人的生计，在我那个年代还没那么严重。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you're at that early, I've raised money.
zh: 但如果你处在那么早期的阶段，我已经融到钱了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got to get to the next raising.
zh: 我得融到下一轮。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got to build this business.
zh: 我得把这个业务做起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got to get some profits and revenue and customers and your reputation and name is wrapped up in that.
zh: 我得做出一些利润、收入和客户，而你的声誉和名字都拴在这上面。

speaker: Unknown
en: I see why this it's incredibly taxing.
zh: 我明白为什么这会让人极度疲惫。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we should start by saying all founders are amazing people that had taken on some insane challenge.
zh: 我想我们应该先说，所有创始人都是很了不起的人，他们承担了某种疯狂的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: They win, they lose, they fail, they succeed.
zh: 他们赢，他们输，他们失败，他们成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're still taking on the same challenge.
zh: 他们仍然在承担同样的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the people that you're talking about that get into it for the wrong reasons, it's very hard to sustain the energy.
zh: 我想你说的那些出于错误原因入行的人，很难持续保持那种能量。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't enjoy creating products or services in whichever industry you're choosing, I don't think you're gonna be able to do it for very long.
zh: 如果你并不享受在你所选的行业里创造产品或服务，我不认为你能坚持很久。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there are very few people that are purely motivated by money or being in the right circles that that's gonna sustain you for a five, 10 year period, right?
zh: 我觉得只有极少数人纯粹被金钱或在正确的圈子里所驱动，而这种驱动力能撑过五年、十年的周期，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you're probably doing this because you really enjoy it.
zh: 我觉得你做这件事可能是因为你真的很享受它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Giving you a microphone and a smart person to talk to, you're like, ah, this is great.
zh: 给你一个麦克风和一个聪明的聊天对象，你会说，啊，这太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dude, I get to interview people like you every day, and it's the most incredible learning thing.
zh: 老兄，我每天都能采访像你这样的人，这是最不可思议的学习方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't care that I get paid.
zh: 我不在乎有没有薪水。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's awesome.
zh: 这太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've figured out what your source of energy is.
zh: 所以你已经搞清楚你的能量来源是什么了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's one of the things, it doesn't have to be the only thing, but it's one of the things that gives you that source of energy.
zh: 这是其中一件事，不必是唯一的事，但它是给你那种能量来源的事情之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think when you, I saw you, you were ranting about this on another one of these walks down the street the other day, and I think it's totally true, but I've been here long enough.
zh: 我想当你……我看到你，前几天在另一个街头漫步节目里你对此大发议论，我觉得完全正确，不过我已经在这一行待了很久了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It sounds like I'm very wise old man, kind of scary.
zh: 听起来我像个很有智慧的老人家，有点吓人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You see this with each of these sort of iterations of the technology industry.
zh: 你会在科技行业的每一轮这样的迭代中看到这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a latest thing that attracts a lot of capital, that attracts a lot of people.
zh: 总有一个最新的东西吸引大量资本，吸引大量人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when that latest thing turned out to be like yesterday's thing, and it still can be incredibly meaningful.
zh: 而当那个最新的东西变成了昨天的东西，它仍然可能具有极其重大的意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: We saw this when mobile took off.
zh: 我们在移动端崛起时见过这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was all these people that arrived to build mobile apps and mobile companies that didn't sustain.
zh: 有很多人涌入去做移动应用和移动公司，却没能持续下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: The ones that won and sustained are often directed in the same area.
zh: 而那些赢下来并持续下来的，往往也是朝着同一个方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: My worry is more that it should be hard, and I completely agree with you on the challenges of founders, but we've made it so normal now for someone to come out, raise 15 million bucks.
zh: 我更大的担忧是，这件事本来应该是难的，我完全同意你对创始人所面临挑战的看法，但我们现在把这一切变得太正常了：一个人出来融个一千五百万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: As a pre-seed, it ain't that fucking hard to raise 15 million bucks now, hire some people, and then honestly play the founder game and then tap out the minute you can.
zh: 作为 pre-seed,现在融一千五百万美元他妈的没那么难，雇几个人，然后说实在的玩玩创始人游戏，一有机会就抽身走人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we've made it too easy in some respects.
zh: 我觉得在某些方面我们把它变得太容易了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's venture capitalists.
zh: 而这就是风险投资家。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a capital society, right?
zh: 这是一个资本社会，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the market price for those types of things.
zh: 这就是那类东西的市场价。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope that people at some point realize working with smart people on difficult problems for long periods of time, the people I work with are a large part of the reason that I'm still doing this, right?
zh: 我希望人们某一天能意识到,长时间和聪明人一起解决困难的问题——我共事的这些人,是我还在做这件事的很大一部分原因,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: The people that we get to create with is the source of energy.
zh: 我们能与之一起创造的人,是能量的来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's
zh: 而我认为那就是

speaker: Unknown
en: Doesn't sound like it's in those people's DNA to do that.
zh: 听起来做那种事不符合那些人的 DNA。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's going to be hard to sustain.
zh: 而这会很难持续。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mike, we're going to do a quick fire because I could talk to you all day.
zh: Mike,我们来快速问答一轮,因为我可以跟你聊一整天。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what have you changed your mind on in the last 12 months most?
zh: 那么在过去 12 个月里,你在什么事情上改变想法最多?

speaker: Unknown
en: The likely future price of inference.
zh: 推理价格未来的可能走向。

speaker: Unknown
en: It goes way down.
zh: 它会大幅下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think so.
zh: 我认为是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Further than I thought.
zh: 比我想的还要低。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does no one say about having money that you think should be said?
zh: 关于有钱这件事,有什么是没人说但你觉得应该说的?

speaker: Unknown
en: That it is a wonderful thing and a big burden at the same time.
zh: 它是一件美妙的事,同时也是一大负担。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is it a big burden, honestly?
zh: 老实说,为什么它是一大负担?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a huge responsibility.
zh: 我认为这是一种巨大的责任。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's just something that's temporarily held as a legacy and you have a responsibility to do, I think, societally profitable things with it.
zh: 我认为它只是暂时被持有的一份遗产,而你有责任用它去做我认为是对社会有益的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Societally profitable, not personally profitable.
zh: 是对社会有益,不是对个人有利。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you feel that burden.
zh: 而我觉得你能感受到那种负担。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's lots of interesting things come with that.
zh: 随之而来的是很多有趣的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do I bring my kids up to not be assholes if they're brought up rich?
zh: 比如,如果孩子们在富有的环境中长大,我该如何把他们培养成不当混蛋的人?

speaker: Unknown
en: Man, ask me in 20 years time.
zh: 天哪,20 年后再问我吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope I get that right.
zh: 我希望我能做对。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, probably try to be yourself.
zh: 我想,大概就是努力做自己吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I read a quote from, I think it was an old Goldman Sachs CEO, says you can tell a lot about people when they get promoted as to whether they grow into the job or swell into it.
zh: 我读到过一句话,我想是某位高盛老 CEO 说的:一个人被提拔时,你能看出很多——他是成长到了这个职位,还是膨胀到了这个职位。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I feel like, man, I've been desperately growing every year I've been in this job and I definitively do not feel like I deserve this job and I have to work crazy hard to deserve it next year or to grow into it or whatever term.
zh: 而我觉得,天哪,我做这份工作的每一年都在拼命成长,而且我绝对不觉得自己配得上这份工作,我必须拼命努力,才能在来年配得上它、成长到它的程度,或者随便什么说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's the same, probably some similar version of this with your kids.
zh: 我想,对孩子大概也是某种类似的版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are curious, if you are humble, if you have gratitude, if you display all those properties, you're probably given the best chance to understand where it is that that comes from.
zh: 如果你有好奇心,如果你保持谦逊,如果你心怀感恩,如果你展现出所有这些品质,你就很可能获得最好的机会,去理解这一切从何而来。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'm sure it's a huge challenge.
zh: 但我确定这会是一个巨大的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell me if you figure it out.
zh: 你要是想明白了告诉我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, I got given some brilliant advice, which is it's just like the National Geographic channel.
zh: 其实,我得到过一条很棒的建议,那就是:就像国家地理频道那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Watch the elephants, the baby elephants, watch the adult elephants and copy them.
zh: 看大象,看小象,看成年大象,然后模仿它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you want your kids to be hardworking and kind, maybe be hardworking.
zh: 所以,如果你想要你的孩子勤劳又善良,也许你自己就要勤劳。

speaker: Unknown
en: Show them that you missed bath time because you were working hard on that Amsterdam trip to make money for the family.
zh: 让他们看到你错过了洗澡时间,因为你在为那次阿姆斯特丹之行努力工作,为家里挣钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And take them to the coffee shop and be really kind to that barista and ask them how their day was.
zh: 带他们去咖啡店,对那位咖啡师非常友善,问问他们今天过得怎么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And let them see that.
zh: 让他们看到这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or if you don't want them to, retire at 45, cheat on your wife and be horrible to the barista and you'll probably have assholes too.
zh: 或者,如果你不想这样,那就 45 岁退休、出轨你的妻子、对咖啡师很恶劣,那你大概也会养出混蛋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're asking, do they copy the way that you act and treat people?
zh: 如果你问的是,孩子会不会模仿你待人接物的方式?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's definitely true.
zh: 我觉得那肯定是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was the advice that I took.
zh: 那就是我所采纳的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the best advice that you've been given?
zh: 你得到过的最好的建议是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: You sit around some pretty interesting tables.
zh: 你坐在不少相当有意思的餐桌旁。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the phrase that I would say, certainly for the last handful of years, I would say, wage peace on yourself.
zh: 我想说的一句话,至少对过去这几年而言,是:对自己讲和,与自己休战。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think lots of things are really hard and having a good attitude and knowing that you tried your best at something, whether it succeeds or doesn't succeed, et cetera, try not to be too hard on yourself if you've done all the right things.
zh: 我觉得很多事情都非常难,而拥有一个好的心态、知道自己在某件事上尽了最大努力——不管它成功还是没成功等等——如果你把所有正确的事都做了,就尽量不要太苛责自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: For a lot of people, especially in the tech industry, their bars on themselves are incredibly high and that can be in its own way a new sort of stress.
zh: 对很多人来说,尤其是在科技行业,他们给自己定的标准高得惊人,而这本身可能以一种新的方式构成一种压力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, touch grass, wait a piece on yourself.
zh: 所以,你知道的,去摸摸草地(回归现实),对自己讲和吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Final one.
zh: 最后一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you not know that you will be capable of achieving that you do need to personally scale?
zh: 有什么是你尚不知道自己有能力做到、而需要你个人去规模化的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd probably say the same thing I said before.
zh: 我大概会说和之前一样的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like how to create moments of slow thinking, moments of slowness in the world that is moving increasingly fast.
zh: 就是如何在这个运转越来越快的世界里创造慢思考的时刻、缓慢的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's going to be a skill that we all need to develop.
zh: 我认为这将是我们都需要培养的一种技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we think the notifications on our phone and the pings from social media and all these sorts of things are distractions, if you're not able to handle that today, I think that the accelerated technological pace, that's going to be really hard.
zh: 如果我们认为手机上的通知和社交媒体的提醒以及所有这些东西都是干扰，如果你今天都无法应对这些，我认为加速的技术节奏会让人非常难以承受。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a real world out there.
zh: 外面有一个真实的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like sometimes in the tech industry, everyone just lives
zh: 就像有时在科技行业里，每个人都只活

speaker: Unknown
en: In a screen like this, ironically, I'm staring at a camera in a screen, right, and all these bits and digits and things, you know, there's a real world out there of stuff that we're creating and slow down to go fast.
zh: 在这样的屏幕里，讽刺的是，我现在正盯着屏幕里的一个摄像头，对吧，还有所有这些比特和数字之类的东西，你知道吗，外面有一个真实的世界，里面是我们正在创造的东西，放慢速度才能跑得更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've got to learn how to slow down and how to really do that, that deep thinking at a time when everything appears to be more fractionalized and speedy.
zh: 我们必须学会如何慢下来，如何在一切都显得更加碎片化和快速的时代真正做到那种深度思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a real challenge.
zh: 这是一个真正的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mike, do you know how I define a good person?
zh: Mike，你知道我如何定义一个好人吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do not.
zh: 不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone who's willing to help with no immediate or clear benefit to themselves of their help being given.
zh: 一个愿意帮助别人，而自己从所提供的帮助中没有即时或明确获益的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've always been incredibly kind to me.
zh: 你一直对我非常友善。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Seriously, I really appreciate it.
zh: 说真的，我非常感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: You haven't needed to, but I really appreciate the relationship.
zh: 你完全没必要这么做，但我真的很珍视这份情谊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, no worries, man.
zh: 嘿，没什么的，兄弟。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anytime.
zh: 随时都在。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me know if I can help.
zh: 如果我能帮上忙就告诉我。

speaker: Unknown
en: But before we leave you today, Base44 is one of those products I used and I just thought straight away, man, I wish I'd had this when I started 20VC with $50 and no contacts in venture.
zh: 但在今天离开你们之前，Base44 是我使用过的产品之一，我立刻就想，天哪，真希望我当初用 50 美元创办 20VC、在风投圈毫无其他人脉的时候就有这个工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wanted to see what it could do, so I built a guest research hub for the show.
zh: 我想看看它能做什么，所以我为这个节目建了一个嘉宾研究中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Upcoming guests, company notes, previous interviews, sponsor contacts, follow-ups, all in one amazing location.
zh: 即将到来的嘉宾、公司笔记、过往访谈、赞助商联系方式、后续跟进，全部集中在一个绝佳的位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: I described it in plain English.
zh: 我用平实的英文描述了需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: A few minutes later, I had the product open in front of me.
zh: 几分钟后，产品就在我面前打开了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Database, login, backend and hosting already handled and just all in one.
zh: 数据库、登录、后端和托管都已处理妥当，而且全都集成在一处。

speaker: Unknown
en: It made it so easy.
zh: 它让这一切变得如此简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what I loved.
zh: 而这正是我喜爱的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't write a long spec.
zh: 我没有写一份冗长的规格说明。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't stitch five different tools together.
zh: 我没有把五个不同的工具拼接在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: I built the thing and I started using it.
zh: 我把东西建了出来，然后就开始用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: For any founder listening, that's the point.
zh: 对于正在收听的任何创始人来说，这就是关键所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: The faster you turn an idea into something real, the faster you launch.
zh: 你越快把一个想法变成真实的东西，你就能越快地推出。
